paper_metadata.title: The as-cast AlxCrTaTi refractory medium entropy alloys with good room-temperature mechanical properties and high-temperature oxidation resistance

evidence.quote: Refractory medium entropy alloys (RMEAs) usually show good mechanical properties at high temperature. Unfortunately, their very poor room-temperature plasticity and high-temperature oxidation resistance still greatly limit their practical application. In this work, the room-temperature mechanical properties and high-temperature oxidation resistance of AlxCrTaTi RMEAs (x = 0, 0.15, 0.25, 0.35) are systematically studied.
AlxCrTaTi refractory medium-entropy alloys with different Al contents were developed

AlxCrTaTi (x = 0, 0.15, 0.25 and 0.35, atomic molar ratio) refractory medium-entropy alloy ingots with different Al contents were prepared through vacuum arc-melting technology by using the high-purity metals (≥99.9 wt%) of Al, Cr, Ta, Ti in a high-purity argon atmosphere.
The alloy rod with 3 mm in diameter and 60 mm in length was fabricated by copper mold suction casting.

Afterwards, the isothermal oxidation experiment was carried out at 1000 °C and the samples were set in the center of the muffle furnace under the experimental environment to be oxidized continuously for 10 h, 25 h, 50 h, and 100 h, respectively. And then all the samples were cooled down to room temperature within the furnace.

The addition of Al promotes the formation of Cr2Ta Laves phase in AlxCrTaTi refractory medium-entropy alloys. With the increase of Al, the Cr2Ta phase gradually increases. In addition, the shape of Cr2Ta phase changes from the rice-grained distribution to gradually growing and lengthening, and finally connecting to each other in the interdendritic region with a spider network.
